Prepare survey data for codebook generation

Source: R/codebook.R
sd_prepare_codebook_data.Rd

The data-preparation half of "06_generoi_codebook.R", pulled out so it can be tested and used on its own without needing the codebook package. Takes an sd_data object and returns a plain data frame with:

  • variable labels and value labels attached as label/labels attributes (the same haven-style convention sd_read() reads them from) — this is what lets codebook show readable descriptions and value labels;

  • automatically detected Likert-item groups turned into <group>_mean scale-score columns, so codebook's reliability calculations (e.g. Cronbach's alpha) have something to work with.

Usage

sd_prepare_codebook_data(x, groups = NULL, min_items = 2)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object.

groups

Optional named list mapping a group name to a character vector of variable names, e.g. list(tt = c("tt1", "tt2", "tt3")). Use this to override automatic detection — for instance when your scale items don't share a numbered-suffix naming pattern. NULL (the default) detects groups automatically.

min_items

Minimum number of variables a detected group must have to be treated as a scale (default 2). Ignored when groups is given explicitly.

Value

A data frame (not an sd_data object) with label/value-label attributes attached and scale-mean columns added, an attribute "sd_groups" recording which groups were used.

Details

Likert groups are detected from variable names that share a common prefix before a trailing number — e.g. tt1, tt2, tt3, tt4 become the group "tt". This generalises the hardcoded tt_mean/joh_mean/imu_mean computation from the original script. Only variables with role "likert" (see sd_detect_roles()) are considered, and a group needs at least min_items members by default — a lone "likert" variable with no siblings is left alone.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aineisto <- sd_read("survey_data.sav")
aineisto <- sd_detect_roles(aineisto)
df <- sd_prepare_codebook_data(aineisto)
attr(df, "sd_groups")
} # }
